title: Haloumi Fingers
subtitle: with Green Bean and Sweet Potato Fries
description: Whether you’re full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they’re packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they’re totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line 2 oven trays with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled sweet potatoes into 1.5cm-thick fries. Trim the beans. Drain the haloumi and dry on paper towel, then slice into fingers.

Bake veggie 'fries': Put the sweet potato on the lined trays. Drizzle with 1 tbs olive oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to coat. Bake for 15 mins. Add the beans to the trays and toss to combine. Swap the position of the trays, then bake for a further 10 mins or until the sweet potato is golden and the beans are tender.

Crumb haloumi: Whisk 1 egg in a shallow bowl. Put 1 tbs plain flour in a separate shallow bowl. Combine the breadcrumbs and barbecue seasoning in a third bowl. Dust the haloumi with the flour, shake off the excess, then dip in the egg and coat in the breadcrumbs.

Fry haloumi fingers: Heat 2 tbs olive oil in a medium frypan over medium heat. Cook the haloumi fingers for 2-3 mins each side until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and drain on paper towel.
Serve up: Divide the haloumi fingers and veggie 'fries' among plates. Serve with the burger sauce for dipping and enjoy!
Did you know?: Did you know? Panko are the Japanese version of breadcrumbs (panko means 'small pieces of bread'). They're lighter and larger than regular breadcrumbs, producing a much better crunch.
